name: Trade war & tariffs
summary: Trump restated on 16 Nov a threat of heavy tariffs on Mexico over migration; no rate, deadline or increase in force
state: On 16 Nov President Trump restated his threat to impose heavy tariffs on Mexico unless it stops migrant flows, without naming a rate or deadline (Newsquawk). It follows his 12 Nov threat to double tariffs on Mexico; Mexican vehicles already face 25% duties and steel and aluminium 50% (KATV). Searches to 18 Nov found no tariff increase in force and no retaliation, so Watch holds: a major rise is threatened but not imposed.
for_you: Tariffs raise costs for importers and can feed through to prices of cars and goods. This describes conditions only.
rubric_hit: New major tariffs threatened between large economies = Watch

sources.title: Newsquawk — Trump reiterates tariff threat to Mexico over migrant flow
KATV — Trump threatens to double tariffs on Mexico if it fails to stop migrant caravan

why: Tariffs raise prices, reroute supply chains and slow growth; escalation cycles hurt export-heavy economies like the UK's partners.
drivers: US tariff policy, retaliation, court rulings, trade deals, WTO disputes.

rubric.alert: Broad new tariffs in force with retaliation under way, or US average effective tariff rising sharply.
rubric.watch: New major tariffs announced or threatened between large economies.
rubric.normal: Tariff regime stable; no new major measures in the past two weeks.
